## Why

Follow-ups raised by the reviewers, UI passes and gates of S258 and S274 (2026-11-07), and the S265/S306 note on this item. Every item was re-anchored against main on 2026-11-18; the ones still open are below, the dropped ones after them. The TUI items touch `internal/tui` and its golden views and the CLI items touch `internal/cli` output, so the slice gets a UI pass (rule u10).

Still open, daemon and CLI:

- A1. The `no_spec_check_row` fix lines build `ork projects set NAME ...` with the bare name (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:165`, `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:177`). Registry names are checked only for non-empty (`internal/registry/registry.go:424-425`), so a name with a space gives a command that cannot be pasted. The TUI already quotes with `engine.ShellWord` (`internal/tui/launch.go:567-569`, `internal/engine/setup.go:63`).
- A2. `matrixUse` labels any row listed in the spec check row set "Spec check row", whatever its role (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:203-209`), but the plan leaves out only reviewer-sourced rows (`internal/daemon/runs.go:648-650`), and `specChain` reads only reviewer rows (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:208-210`). An implementer row id in `spec_check_rows` is labelled a Spec check row and still runs as an implementer.
- A3. A row in both the UI pass set and the spec check set: the plan drops it as a spec check row first (`internal/daemon/runs.go:648-656`), the matrix labels it "UI pass row" first (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:204-207`).
- A4. `spec_check_rows` that take every reviewer row leave the reviewer chain empty, and `planRun` returns a plain `fmt.Errorf` ("lineup has no row with an adapter for reviewer", `internal/daemon/runs.go:666-671`) that has no ipc code, so the owner sees it as internal.
- A5. Stale comments: `SpecCheckRows` says unset means "the row that the Spec check row rule names" (`internal/registry/registry.go:278-281`), but it is every row any rule names, in rule order (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:105-115`); the `matrixUse` comment says the UI pass and Spec check rows are rows "that a rule names" (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:182-186`), but project settings name them too.
- B1. `ork answer --wait` and `ork retry --wait` return at once when the resume waits for a slot: the stored-resume path returns before the `NoWait` check (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2433-2449` against `internal/daemon/runs.go:2453-2458`). Open owner question: `cli.wait-queued-resume`.
- B2. A stop that cancels an answer already filed in adj: the reply is the job's `context canceled` error (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2484-2490`), and the client shows the error, not the filing notice carried in `Message`.
- B3. The waiting-path adj filing runs under the request context (`fileWaitingAnswerLocked(ctx, ...)`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:2117-2121`), so a client that disconnects can leave a key asked but not decided.
- C1. `ork projects set --allow` adds patterns (adj 190), but the summary prints only each role's total pattern count (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:756-771`, `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:787-791`), not how many were added or were already listed.
- C2. An older TUI or CLI binary against a restarted daemon gets "plan changed; run the command again to confirm it" (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1056`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1156`) on any plan with warnings. No upgrade note says so.

Still open, TUI:

- T1. The Waves launch goes from `confirmWave` to the spec check and then the confirm (`internal/tui/waves.go:305-313`) without the `check: none` line and the adj 191 (`launch.no-check-command`) refusal that the launch confirm shows before y (`internal/tui/launch.go:555-570`). The daemon error comes afterwards and suggests `--allow-no-check`, which the TUI cannot pass.
- T2. The launch confirm clips the warnings and the note below the roles at 80x24 behind "+N more lines" (`window`, `internal/tui/view.go:1093-1108`), and the confirm takes every key, so they cannot be scrolled to.
- T3. The refusal for t or an answer on a run whose resume waits, "resume already waits for a slot; ork stop RUN cancels it" (`internal/tui/model.go:1829-1832`), wraps with one word alone on its second line at 80 columns with a real run id.
- T4. The Running heard cell reads `wait 20m` from when the wait began (`heardCell`, `internal/tui/relayboard.go:154-161`), not from when the resume was queued; the record has `Resume.At` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2434`) but `EngineRun` carries only `ResumeWaiting` and `WaitStartedAt` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2877`).
- T5. At 80x24 the pane hint of a run whose resume waits loses `x stop`, the only action left for it (drop order in `internal/tui/keys.go:213-228`).
- T6. An unselected row of a run whose resume waits has no cue beside `wait 20m`: `resumeWaiting` is set on the row (`internal/tui/overview.go:67`, `internal/tui/overview.go:443`) but no row renderer reads it.

Dropped on 2026-11-18, with evidence:

- `spec_check_rows` after a shared matrix renumbers rows: S261 (open, "Shared role matrix") rewrites row ids in the target project; it belongs there.
- A failed registry read admits answer and retry on the last good file: the same rule as every queued start (`loadRunRegistryLocked`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1819-1826`, used by `launchRun` at `internal/daemon/runs.go:2178-2182`). No change.
- `engineRuns` reads the registry once per waiting run under the manager lock (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2794`): cost only, no observed problem.
- "Long refusal and status lines overflow 80 columns with real run ids": no line named beyond T3, and the review called them consistent with existing ones.
- `TestDoctorCheckCommandSyntaxError` on Linux: it passes on this Linux host on 2026-11-18 (it lowercases the output, `internal/cli/cli_test.go:1039-1044`).
- The Codex implementer's missing host binary: host setup, not ork code.
